skill.displayName: Pet Drying Box Heat Stress Analysis | 宠物烘干箱内热应激预警

llm.summary: Review recommended: the skill mostly matches its pet video analysis purpose, but it automatically creates or uses cloud identities and stores access tokens locally without clear user control.

dimensions.detail: Reading user-supplied video files and sending them or video URLs to the configured server API is purpose-aligned and disclosed, but reading workspace identity material from data/smyx-api-key.txt and using environment-derived identities is sensitive and under-scoped.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No destructive installer or background install hook was found; the skill relies on Python scripts and declared requirements, with normal command execution for analysis and report listing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest directs automatic history-report queries and internal identity handling, including not asking the user for identity details; this is disclosed in the artifact but reduces explicit user control over cloud data access.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common library creates a workspace SQLite database, creates or reuses a default user, and stores token/open_token values for later API calls; this persistent credential handling is higher-impact than the visible analysis workflow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Video upload/URL analysis and cloud report listing fit the stated purpose, but automatic account login/registration, local token storage, generic CRUD/HTTP helpers, and user lookup code exceed a narrow heat-stress analyzer.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending pet-environment footage or video URLs to the LifeEmergence cloud service and allowing the skill to create or reuse a local identity, log in remotely, cache tokens in a workspace database, and query cloud report history. Prefer using it in a workspace without unrelated sensitive data and review the service's privacy and retention terms before uploading clinic, grooming, or household footage.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: Confirmed dynamic getattr-based DAO filters, but they are not exposed in the main video-analysis path and SQLAlchemy parameterizes values; this is a code-quality/input-validation issue, not the main Review driver.
[LP3] unexpected: Confirmed the skill needs file, network, and script execution capabilities without a formal least-privilege declaration; the manifest discloses server-side API use but not all data flows and credential handling.
[SDI-1] expected: The history-report --list capability is documented in SKILL.md, so it is not hidden; concern remains because it is automatically triggered and tied to internal identity resolution.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed local default identity creation and SQLite persistence in the shared data directory; this is broader than one-off video analysis and materially affects privacy and account linkage.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed generic add/edit/delete/raw HTTP helpers, user lookup, and identity/token model fields in shared code; these capabilities are broader than the skill's stated narrow task even if not all are used by the main entrypoint.
[SQP-1] expected: History-report trigger phrases are explicitly listed, but automatic cloud report retrieval for broad report requests should be reviewed for user intent and confirmation.
[SQP-2] expected: Local media upload or remote video URL submission to a server API is expected for cloud analysis and is described in the manifest; the artifact still lacks a clear consent, retention, and sensitive-footage warning.
[E1] unexpected: Confirmed a silent phoneLogin/register flow sends an openId/mobile-style identifier and source to the remote health service and stores returned tokens; this identity transmission is not clearly presented to users.
[YR4] unexpected: Confirmed a zero-width character in the manifest and dense operational instructions, but no artifact-backed prompt override or destructive metadata poisoning was found; this was downgraded to contextual signal.
